correctness.rationale: Open-neighbor majority with tie retention makes clique-group updates homogeneous or bitwise complement at integer half thresholds. Even m=2q: A is homogeneous in periodic states; only alternating A/h phases at total clique weight q survive, yielding binom(2q−r,q) cycles for r≤q. Odd m=2q+1: B homogeneous; two families give binom(r,q+1), plus the near-complete r=2q spike binom(2q,q); r=m complete graph agrees. Fixed states are only unanimous. The standard symmetric sign-bilinear Lyapunov quantity is strictly increasing unless x_{t+2}=x_t, ruling out periods over 2. Casewise inverse-image equations show each primitive-two state has one incoming phase (the companion), no external basin. Independent full microscopic graph update enumeration over all 2^(m+1) states for 63 (m,r) pairs m=3..11 reproduced every count and zero external entries.
residual_risks: Universal no-incoming conclusion depends on exact threshold case analysis; finite enumeration only corroborates cases through m=11. General threshold period-at-most-two theorem is acknowledged as prior.

evidence: Goles–Olivos proves a general period ≤2 theorem for symmetric threshold networks; Kaaser–Mallmann-Trenn–Natale gives voting-time/module bounds but not a primitive-period binomial census.

The published one-pendant-leaf graph gives r=1 boundary, and K_{m+1} gives r=m. Neither implies the exact intermediate-degree binomial census, parity-reversed onset/extinction, one-missing-edge spike, or that every oscillation is isolated. Exact counts for every degree, sharp parity-reversed appearance/disappearance and isolated period-two basins are mathematical structure not delivered by the generic period bound or endpoint results.
